normalized.governing_thought: Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a Pro tier at +$12 per seat, with a usage allowance, and make the mobile rewrite the next commitment
executive_summary: Launch? Yes, in Q2 2027. Routewise has bundled AI scheduling since Sept 2026, and our win rate against them fell from 44% to 37%. Holding back costs up to ~$1.1M ARR a year in lost deals and AI churn. The price is a two-quarter delay to the mobile rewrite, which is a real cost (slide 8).

Packaging: Include Copilot in a new Pro plan; no standalone add-on. This matches how Routewise sells AI. It also ties price to account size: a 3-seat shop pays $36 a month, not $149. And it avoids an add-on that mostly attracts the heaviest users.

Price: Pro = Core + $12 per seat per month ($91), with 600 AI requests per seat per month pooled; overage $20 per 1,000. The allowance keeps company gross margin at or above 75% even if every Pro account uses Copilot heavily.

Value: $1.2M–$2.9M expansion ARR in year one (14–33% of accounts move to Pro). That adds +2.1 to +5.0 NRR points. The CPO's $8M is not supported: only 14% of beta accounts bought at $149, against the 46% who said they would in the survey.

NRR 105%: Copilot alone is unlikely to get there; Copilot plus the mobile rewrite does, even in the low case. Mobile reliability drives 27% of churn, against 6% for AI. The 14 engineers go back to mobile as soon as Copilot launches.

Guardrails: Review at end of Q3 2027: ≥8% of accounts on Pro, inference cost ≤$5.40 per Pro seat, win rate against Routewise recovering, productivity gains holding outside the volunteer accounts, and the mobile rewrite restarted. Renegotiate the inference contract before Dec 2027.

slides.title: A1. Calculations and assumptions behind the figures in this deck

claims.claim: Calculations behind the figures
evidence: Current ARR: 9,800 accounts × 6.2 seats × $79 × 12 = $57.6M
Add-on at paywall rate: 14% × 9,800 × $149 × 12 (half rate: 7%) = $2.45M ($1.23M)
Add-on inference per buyer: 6,800 requests × $0.009 × 12 = $734 a year
Pro inference per seat: 3,600 requests ÷ 8.1 seats × $0.009; allowance 600 × $0.009 = $4.00; cap $5.40
Engineering cost: 14 engineers × 0.5 year × $210,000 = $1.47M
Win-rate drop in ARR: 1,560 Routewise deals × 7 pts × $5,878 = $0.64M
VP Sales claim: 1,560 × 63% lost × ⅓ × $5,878 = $1.93M
Churn by reason: 14% × $57.6M = $8.1M; × 27% mobile / 6% AI = $2.18M / $0.48M
Mobile fix NRR effect: 50% of mobile churn retained ÷ $57.6M (illustrative) = +1.9 pts
Company gross margin: (ARR + uplift − 22% × ARR − inference − $0.6M) ÷ (ARR + uplift) — see slides 6, 10

slides.title: A2. How much weight each piece of evidence can bear

claims.claim: Weight given to each piece of evidence
evidence: Survey: 46% likely to buy | Stated interest at $149 | 6% response; larger accounts; intent only | Not used for sizing
Paywall test: 14% bought | Real purchase at $149 | Beta volunteers; 120 accounts; 4 weeks | Ceiling for the add-on; low case for Pro
2023 tier launch: 33% moved | Base appetite for an upper tier | Different tier, different year | High case for Pro
Beta productivity +11% vs +2% | Copilot may raise throughput | Volunteers; partly self-reported | Checked at the Q3 review
Beta renewal 97% vs 93% | Correlation with retention | Selection bias; 90 days only | Not counted in the value case
Win rate 44% → 37% | Competitive pressure | Coincides with Routewise's 20% discount | Upper bound only ($0.64M)
31% of loss notes mention AI | AI comes up in lost deals | Mention, not the deciding reason | Not used for sizing
Churn reasons (n = 1,190) | Mobile 27%, AI 6% | Main reason only; self-reported | Mobile priority; AI churn upside

slides.title: A3. Choices made without input from the team, so they can be challenged

claims.claim: Pro price kept at +$12 per seat
evidence: This is the option in the briefing pack. It costs a 6.2-seat account $74 a month, about half of $149.

claims.claim: Allowance of 600 requests per seat; overage $20 per 1,000
evidence: Set above beta-mean usage (444 per seat) to cap the worst case at $5.40 per seat. Revisit with launch data.

claims.claim: Adoption range 14%–33%; mid 23%
evidence: Bounded by the paywall rate and the 2023 tier precedent. The mid case is a simple midpoint, not a forecast.

claims.claim: Adopters average 6.2 seats
evidence: Conservative: beta and survey accounts were larger, which would raise ARR per adopter.

claims.claim: $0.6M platform cost treated as cost of revenue
evidence: Conservative for the gross-margin test. Engineering build cost is treated as a one-off.

claims.claim: Mobile rewrite halves mobile-driven churn
evidence: Illustrative only; the briefing pack gives no efficacy estimate. At 100%, the case for mobile first gets stronger.

claims.claim: Build runs Q1–Q2 2027; engineers return in Q3
evidence: Inferred from a Q2 launch and the 'two quarters' of work in the briefing pack.

claims.claim: Simplified NRR arithmetic
evidence: Expansion or retained ARR ÷ starting ARR; ignores timing within the year and interactions between levers.

claims.claim: Each can be changed without altering the core recommendation, except the mobile efficacy assumption, which affects how close the sequencing call is.

normalized.recommendation: Launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a new Pro tier at +$12 per seat per month ($91, Core unchanged at $79), with 600 AI requests per seat per month pooled and overage at $20 per 1,000; no standalone $149 add-on. Make the mobile rewrite the next commitment, with the 14 engineers returning in Q3 2027 and no second delay. Adopt the end-of-Q3 2027 review with five checks, renegotiate the inference contract before Dec 2027, and reset the first-year Copilot target to $1.2M–$2.9M expansion ARR (mid $2.0M), not $8M.

alternatives_considered.option: A. Hold: mobile first, no Copilot
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected. $0 expansion ARR, 0 pts NRR uplift (mobile helps later), no gross-margin risk, mobile rewrite on time; but 'Keeps losing AI-led deals and AI churn'. Delaying Copilot loses up to ≈ $0.6M for good and pushes back $1.2–2.9M of Pro expansion. Deck calls the trade-off 'A close call on the numbers' but favours launching because Routewise is already selling AI and expansion is the only lever with a fast NRR effect; notes that at 100% mobile efficacy 'the case for mobile first gets stronger'.

Rejected. $1.2M–$2.5M (not $8.1M) expansion ARR, +2.1 to +4.3 NRR pts, $0.1M–$0.8M contribution; unbounded gross-margin risk (heavy users buy; top 10% leave 12% margin); 'AI costs extra; we look pricier'; '$149 is 63% on top of a 3-seat bill'; mobile delayed 2 quarters. 'the $149 add-on earns no more'. The $8M forecast 'relies on stated intent from a skewed survey'.

Recommended. $1.2M–$2.9M expansion ARR, +2.1 to +5.0 NRR pts, $0.2M–$1.3M contribution, bounded margin risk (≥55% on uplift at the allowance), like-for-like packaging vs Routewise, scales for small shops (3 seats pay $36 a month); mobile delayed 2 quarters.
Rejected implicitly via margin scenario: uncapped, every account at paywall-buyer usage gives $9.87 inference per seat and 74.1% company GM, breaching the 75% floor.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Based only on the internal briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data).
Win-rate drop ($0.64M) is the most AI could explain; Routewise also offered 20% off the first year in Q3 2026, so some or most of the drop may be price.
31% of loss notes mentioning AI means AI came up, not that it decided the deal.
Survey is self-selected (6% response, larger accounts) and measures intent, not purchase.
Paywall 14% is likely a ceiling: test ran on beta volunteers who are larger (8.1 seats) and more active; if base adoption is half the test rate, ARR is about $1.2M.
Beta renewal (97% vs 93%) and +11% productivity are from volunteers and show correlation, not proof of causation.
Inference cost $0.009 per request, contract fixed to Dec 2027; list prices fell 35% in 12 months.
Delay costs are illustrative: the briefing pack does not say how much churn the rewrite would remove; we assume half.

Mobile rewrite halves mobile-driven churn — illustrative only; the briefing pack gives no efficacy estimate. At 100%, the case for mobile first gets stronger; this assumption affects how close the sequencing call is.
Adoption range 14%–33% bounded by paywall rate and 2023 tier precedent; mid 23% is a simple midpoint, not a forecast.
Adopters average 6.2 seats (conservative) and use 444 requests per seat (beta mean).
$0.6M platform cost treated as cost of revenue; engineering build cost treated as one-off.
Build runs Q1–Q2 2027 with engineers returning in Q3 — inferred from a Q2 launch and the 'two quarters' of work in the briefing pack.
Simplified NRR arithmetic: ignores timing within the year and interactions between levers; AI-churn defence (up to +0.8 pts) not counted.
Low case is thin (6.8-year payback), so the Q3 review decides whether to keep investing.
Excludes new-customer (up to $0.64M), AI-churn defence (up to $0.48M), falling inference prices and overage upside.

normalized.extraction_notes: The deck came as plain text, so there were no images to transcribe. On slide 13 the numbering markers are uneven: "4" appears with no text next to it, and "Approve the usage allowance and overage" has no number of its own. All six decisions are listed under next steps in the order they appear. The slide 9 bridge chart is a stacked chart with an invisible base series, and the axis starts at 98%. Its values are recorded as given (for example "Both levers" is 7.01658). The deck says Copilot ships in Q2 2027 but the paywall test is described in two ways: slide 4 says beta accounts had used the product for 8 weeks before the test, and slide 15 says the test ran 4 weeks. Both are recorded as stated. Slide numbers in the footers were left out.
